title: Unload a kernel module
summary: You can remove a loaded kernel module from the kernel if it is no longer needed or is causing issues.

steps.explain: Use sudo rmmod followed by the module name to remove it from the kernel.

placeholders.name: MODULE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the kernel module to unload.

alternatives.explain: Alternatively, use modprobe with the -r flag.

placeholders.name: MODULE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the kernel module to unload.

rollback.explain: To reload the module, use modprobe.

placeholders.name: MODULE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the kernel module to load.

warnings: You cannot unload a module if it is currently in use by another module or process.
